So refreshing to hear from someone who hasn't gone completely insane.....

The content is exactly what I needed I really appreciate the effort.

I'm so glad we have Greg. It saddens me that you have to go through this

This matches my experience using LLM code review tools, they will create 8 PR comments per actual bug in the code (even if the same LLM wrote the code!)

Greg is just such a likeable person, I've been sitting next to him on some Linux conference 15 years ago, we didn't talk much but he definitely is cool. Thankful he still goes strong.

Absolutely worth watching.

I think the real challenge for people is that it’s now trivially easy for someone to BS them. These marketing claims resonate because more people are now easy targets. In the past, only con artists could con. You had to clear a certain bar. Now AI can, well, make art. And it’s really up to people with taste and discrimination to see through it. I can’t say I’m perfect here; I’ve definitely accepted bugs and had too much code churn. Increasingly it feels like I’m bottlenecked just triaging mostly-slop.

I'm also happy to live in the EU, and let America do all the hardware innovation and we have nice careers on top of it.

This is one of the best talks I've seen from one of the smartest minds, with access to cutting edge models like Mythos. His experience in dealing with LLM's mirrors my own - lots of midwits who think their slop cannon is smart. It's a capable technology, its not nearly as capable as they want it to be with their copium. Maybe because its smarter than them they think its smart? I don't know. I don't understand the AI clowns who shovel 33 PR's filled with random garbage on a project and expect anyone to even read their work when they haven't even looked at it themselves. I guess they expect our slop bots to just sign off on it?

Keeping "hallucination" out of the AI lexicon is a great idea, as you said, it's lending too much credit to the LLM. I recently have had Codex and Claude both outright lie to me- just made things up entirely that never existed then it tried to tell me I was somehow the reason for that. That's not a hallucination, if that were a person I would never say "you're hallucinating", I would say "you're a liar".

Very good talk! But he keeps repeating "do not panic", which is not what you say when you don't want ppl to panic lol :D I thought he would talk about copy fail though. From what I remember, I think the devs that reported the bug did not realise that the kernel security team would not take care of coordinating with the distros. That resulted in the distros being caught off guard. That CVE was found with the help of llms and it was a nasty one indeed :(

Lol wtf are we doing in modern software!?!? Creating ourselves a nightmare of nonsensical busy work it seems.

Because a large amount of inaccurate and unscientific information that has accumulated over time has not been corrected in a timely manner, this has led to issues regarding AI safety.

You clearly enjoy what you do.

While I am glad that GKH is at least working at this, the CNA stuff is particularly egregious. I'm concerned by what I'm seeing following the grsec patches via Brad Spengler. There are so many flaws in the way the kernel folks interact with those who actually work to improve security....!

12:46six seveeeen (sorri)

There’s a huge disconnect between the factual content of what he is saying and the sneering dismissal of the delivery

"If you have a malicious user on your desktop that has access to your GPU they can do much worse things than this" Okay, I'm sure clouds that rent out GPUs by the second will be pleased to hear that I hate how so many us just inject straight copium into our veins to downplay security vulnerabilities I hate how we always try to come up with fraudulent reasonings on why bugs don't matter or why usecases don't exist Nobody has less clue how software is being used than the narrow-minded programmer who made it for himself Thank goodness they're still fixing small bugs. But this isn't about linux or Greg in particular. I'm pissed off at the general programming community because this train of thought is rampant and harmful Your network card runs arbitrary code if it encounters a malformed packet if it gets edited in the middle of the network stack, "Umm ackchually it's not possible to do X, it's not a real bug!" Just fix the damn parsing and shut up... Just spend time making the code correct instead of spending time coming up with reasons why it doesn't matter if it stays incorrect. You're wrong half the time. You don't know.

The cope here is real. I understand the moral issues but you should be able to separate morality from the issue at hand. What you are looking at is old tech and it will never get worse than this. It will improve while we will not. That is the main issue: you as a human will not get better. You don’t have to worry about critical bugs being sent to you.. it’s the ones that are not. 50% hit rate is insanely good. I am completely flabbergasted you don’t see this. When does it become an issue? At 60%? 70%? Does it matter? “They” are not writing comments like that. Claude had some issues with this but others don’t. It changes a lot with the settings, context, skills, etc. There is no mention of models, reasoning efforts, harnessing.. it is not at all encouraging to see people in this position being so badly informed about AI (“LLM” is one of them, yes). “Pattern matchers” is thrown around without any substantiation. It is bordering misinformation. You are a pattern matcher as well? You want to get into the philosophical issues? Really? Why?
